title: Committee of Supply – Head R (Ministry of Law)
what_it_is: Committee of Supply – Head R (Ministry of Law)

sections.label: MinLaw pandemic business legislation measures
sections.summary: The Ministry of Law led legislative measures to help small and micro-businesses during the pandemic, including contract relief, rental relief, insolvency and re-align frameworks.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Since the pandemic hit us, the Ministry of Law spearheaded the implementation of a slew of legislative measures aimed at helping small and micro-businesses.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Measures included the Temporary Relief for Inability to Perform Contracts, Rental Relief Framework, Simplified Insolvency Programme and the Re-align Framework.

sections.label: Will-making rates Singapore and UK
sections.summary: A 2017 Straits Times article reported only 10%-15% of Singaporeans made wills, versus over 40% in the UK in 2017.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
sentences.text: In the Straits Times article published in July 2017, it was reported that only 10%-15% of Singaporeans have made wills.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
sentences.text: In contrast, it was reported that in 2017, the corresponding figure in UK is more than 40%.

sections.label: Digital wills for Singaporeans
sections.summary: Technological advancement should allow options for Singaporeans to execute digital wills kept securely and acted upon after the testator's death per their wishes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
sentences.text: With the technological advancement we have made since, we should be able to provide options for Singaporeans to execute digital wills, ensuring that the wills are kept securely and acted upon upon the death of the testator in accordance with his or her wishes.

sections.label: Criminal legal aid access review
sections.summary: There is still a need to enhance access to justice and criminal legal aid for deserving accused persons, and MinLaw was reviewing criminal legal aid including a possible Public Defender's Office.

sentences.speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Notwithstanding, there is still a need to enhance access to justice and to improve the provision of criminal legal aid for deserving accused persons who do not have the means to afford their own lawyers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I note that the Minister for Law said in Parliament last year that MinLaw was conducting a review of criminal legal aid, including the possibility of setting up a Public Defender's Office.

sections.label: Support for vulnerable groups access
sections.summary: The speaker asks the Minister for Law how MinLaw will support access to justice for vulnerable groups given COVID-19, and for an update on the criminal legal aid review.

sentences.speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In this regard, I would like to ask the Minister for Law how does MinLaw intend to provide more support for enhancing access to justice for vulnerable groups, especially given the impact of COVID-19, and if there is an update on MinLaw’s review of criminal legal aid, including when MinLaw expects the review to be completed?

sections.label: Family violence definition and legal aid
sections.summary: The speaker asks whether the Women's Charter's "family violence" definition could become "domestic violence" covering intimate partner and household violence, and asks progress on the Public Defender's Office.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Would the Ministry consider the replacement of the definition of "family violence" in the Women’s Charter with "domestic violence" to include intimate partner violence and violence against others in a household notwithstanding the lack of any familial relationship?

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, during the debate on the Parti Liyani’s case, the Minister for Law has mentioned the possibility to increase legal aid for the economically vulnerable.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: We would like to know what is the progress in setting up the Public Defender’s Office?

sections.label: Means test and legal aid
sections.summary: A resident faces a choice between staying with a care-giving family member or living separately to keep means test access to legal aid.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: My resident told me he faces an invidious choice – stay with a family member who can provide care-giving support or choose to stay separately without the family member as care-giver in order to maintain his means test access to legal aid.

sections.label: Public Defender's Office evaluation
sections.summary: The Ministry is evaluating considerations for a potential Public Defender's Office, and the speaker supports making legal information more accessible.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Often, when the need strikes, they are at a loss and this could be during a time where there is family violence, death or trauma.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: I am glad that the Ministry is evaluating the considerations for a potential Public Defender's Office and support the efforts to make legal information more accessible.

sections.label: Digital legal information infrastructure
sections.summary: The Ministry could work with agencies to build digital infrastructure so more people gain basic legal knowledge and seek advice virtually.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: And since the circuit breaker, the Law Society Pro Bono Services have been sharing a series of "Know the Law" webinars on YouTube and its Community Legal Clinics have also begun providing legal advice to residents in need via virtual platforms.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: It would therefore be helpful if the Ministry can consider working with these agencies and stakeholders to build up the digital infrastructure, with the goal of enabling more people to have better basic knowledge on common legal issues, such as consumer rights and estate planning; and seek for legal advice when necessary via virtual platforms.

sections.label: Community Dispute Resolution Tribunal
sections.summary: The Community Dispute Resolution Tribunal has been in place since 2015.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: The Community Dispute Resolution Tribunal has been in place since 2015.

sections.label: Doxing cases and POHA
sections.summary: The speaker asks whether many doxing cases have been filed since POHA was amended and whether the Ministry assessed POHA's effectiveness.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: Has there been many cases against doxing filed in the courts since POHA was amended?

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: Has Ministry of Law made any assessment about the effectiveness of POHA since the Act was amended in 2019?

sections.label: CMC mediation recommendations
sections.summary: The speaker proposes mandatory attendance at CMC mediation, full-time professional mediators, and binding agreements enforceable through the CDRT.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: First, when a resident chooses to lodge an application for mediation, the CMC should mandate that both parties be present at the mediation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Second, the CMC should be staffed with full time, professional mediators to mediate cases.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Third, agreements must be binding on all parties.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: If violated, the complainant should be able to use it to file a case with the CDRT for a fast track application for an injunction.

sections.label: Ministry advancing unpaid wages
sections.summary: A suggestion is that the Ministry of Manpower can advance money for unpaid wages and stand in as preferred creditor.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan
sentences.text: One suggestion in the context of an insolvent company, is that the Ministry of Manpower can advance money to pay part of the worker’s unpaid wages and then stand in place of the worker as a preferred creditor to recover the advanced monies upon distribution of the insolvent company’s assets.

sections.label: Ministry of Law technology initiatives
sections.summary: The Ministry of Law set a technology vision with the Technology and Innovation Roadmap and introduced Tech Start and Tech-celerate for Law.

sentences.speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas
sentences.text: The Ministry of Law had set overall vision and blueprint for technology and innovation for law firms with the launch of the Technology and Innovation Roadmap in October 2020.

sentences.speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas
sentences.text: The Ministry of Law has also introduced technology adoption initiatives such as Tech Start for Law and Tech-celerate for Law.

sections.label: Lawyers Go Global programmes
sections.summary: The Ministry of Law has been proactive with programmes like Lawyers Go Global and the China Ready Programme.

sentences.speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas
sentences.text: The Ministry of Law has been proactive with programmes like Lawyers Go Global, and the China Ready Programme for lawyers.

sections.label: Helping small and medium law firms
sections.summary: The question asks how the Ministry can help lawyers from small- and medium-sized firms stay relevant and thrive.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: My question is therefore, how can the Ministry help lawyers from small- and medium-sized firms stay relevant and continue to thrive in the changing legal landscape?

sections.label: Entity for technology consultancy
sections.summary: The question asks whether an entity could be created for firms to avail themselves of technology consultancy services.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: Would it be possible to create an entity with such firms could avail themselves to technology consultancy services to help develop the IT infrastructure?

sections.label: Singapore international disputes resolution hub
sections.summary: The speaker shared views on promoting Singapore as an international disputes resolution hub and noted Singapore Convention on Mediation signatories and SMC figures.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, I have shared my view with this House on promoting Singapore on an international disputes resolution hub, particularly, in the areas of mediation and arbitration.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: I also filed a Parliamentary Question recently and am pleased to note that the Singapore Convention on Mediation, also known as the United Nations Convention on International Settlement Agreements Resulting from Mediation, which entered into force on 12 September 2020, now has 53 signatories, including the world's two largest economies, the United States and China, and other large Asian economies such as India and South Korea.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: Based on information from its website, the SMC is said to have mediated more than 4,800 matters worth over $10 billion since its launch in 1997.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: About 70% of SMC mediated cases are settled, with 90% of those cases settled within one day.

sections.label: SIAC New York office
sections.summary: In 2020, the SIAC opened its first representative office outside Asia, in New York.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: In 2020, the SIAC opened its first representative office outside of Asia, in New York.

sections.label: Hague Service Convention accession
sections.summary: The speaker suggests the Government consider acceding to the Hague Service Convention on service abroad of judicial and extrajudicial documents.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
sentences.text: To further improve the framework, I suggest the Government consider acceding to the Hague Service Convention, which is the short form for the Convention on the Service Abroad of Judicial and Extrajudicial Documents in Civil or Commercial Matters.

sections.label: IP protection regime balance
sections.summary: Singapore seeks a strong IP protection regime, but must calibrate it given barriers such as the COVID-19 vaccine race.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
sentences.text: In tandem with that reputation, we strive to provide a strong regime of intellectual property (IP) protection within our jurisdiction and have consistently ranked among the top in the world.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
sentences.text: A strong IP regime provides an incentive framework in which innovation can be encouraged.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
sentences.text: However, IP protection can be a barrier in extreme circumstances such as what we currently face in the race for vaccines against COVID-19.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
sentences.text: Hence, we must find the right approach, calibrated to Singapore's context, to affirm companies and inventors that their IP is safe here and can be defended in the event a dispute arises out of IP rights such as patents.

sections.label: SLA data platforms and digitisation
sections.summary: The question asks what plans SLA has for data platforms and digitising documentation-intensive processes like conveyancing using smart contracts and distributed ledger technology.

sentences.speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: With the digital efforts undertaken across Government agencies, what plans does the SLA have in making available data platforms for businesses and individuals to make better decisions?

sentences.speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: For documentation intensive processes, will SLA consider digitising more in these areas, such as conveyancing-related processes using smart contracts and distributed ledger technology?

sections.label: Community Mediation Centre mediators
sections.summary: 80% of CMC-mediated cases reach amicable settlement, and all 147 mediators completed training, with new ones SIMI-accredited since 2018.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: Members may know that 80% of cases that are mediated at the Community Mediation Centre (CMC) have reached an amicable settlement.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: All 147 of CMC's mediators have completed mediation training and assessment, before being appointed.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: Since 2018, all new mediators must be accredited by the Singapore International Mediation Institute (SIMI).

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: And they must complete 12 hours of additional training during their three-year term to be re-appointed.

sections.label: Community dispute management review
sections.summary: An inter-agency committee of MinLaw, MCCY, MND and MHA has begun a comprehensive review of the community dispute management framework.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: These disputes often sit somewhere between being an annoyance and an offence, and the resolution of these disputes often require a multi-faceted approach.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: So, an inter-agency committee involving the Ministry of Law, MCCY, MND and MHA has commenced a comprehensive review of the community dispute management framework to address these challenges.

sections.label: Special Directions and CDRT claims
sections.summary: 24 Special Directions and two Exclusion Orders were issued, and 591 claims were filed since the CDRT began on 1 October 2015.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: A total of 24 Special Directions have been issued as at 31 December 2020, for these egregious cases, and to date, two Exclusion Orders have been made.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: Since the CDRT was operationalised on 1 October 2015, 591 claims have been filed as of the end of last year, 31 December 2020.

sections.label: Protection Orders filed under POHA
sections.summary: 853 Protection Orders were filed since POHA came into force on 15 November 2014.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: Since POHA came into force on 15 November 2014, 853 Protection Orders (POs) have been filed as of end of last year.

sections.label: Mediation and expedited Protection Orders
sections.summary: Of 853 PO applications, 135 went to mediation and 366 expedited POs were granted, about four in 10 applications.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: Of the 853 PO applications filed, 135 were sent for mediation 366 expedited POs were granted this means that the court granted interim relief in roughly about four out of 10 applications.

sections.label: Doxxing cases in State Courts
sections.summary: As of 31 December 2020, 29 doxxing cases were filed in the State Courts.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: As of 31 December 2020, there were 29 cases of doxxing filed in the State Courts.

sections.label: Lending to foreigners reduced
sections.summary: These measures significantly reduced lending to foreigners, especially the more vulnerable, and kept indebtedness under control.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: As a result of these measures, lending to foreigners, especially the more vulnerable ones has reduced significantly and indebtedness has been kept under control.

sections.label: Moneylending licence pilot programme
sections.summary: Six firms received moneylending licences in 2019 to pilot new business models, with the programme ending in 2022 for assessment.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: We continue to look for ways to better protect borrowers such as through business-led improvements.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: So, for example in 2019, we granted moneylending licences to six firms to pilot new business models with features such as more comprehensive use of data, to enhance credit worthiness assessment and also digitalised processes.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: This pilot programme will end in 2022, following which, we will assess its impact on the industry and it will inform our efforts to enhance the moneylending regulatory regime.

sections.label: Government co-funding Enhanced CLAS
sections.summary: The Government has co-funded Enhanced CLAS since 2015, funding on average $2 million yearly, about 75% of CLAS' operating costs.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: The Government has been co-funding the Criminal Legal Aid Scheme, or CLAS, what we call "Enhanced CLAS" since 2015, to serve more accused persons who merit legal assistance but cannot afford it.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: The Government funds on average $2 million per year, that is about 75% of CLAS' total operating costs.

sections.label: Review of criminal legal aid model
sections.summary: A review of the criminal legal aid model began in 2019 and will conclude this year, covering means criteria, offences and a possible Public Defender's Office.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: As stated in the Ministerial Statement on Parti Liyani v Public Prosecutor last November, we started reviewing our criminal legal aid model in 2019, five years since the start of the Enhanced CLAS.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: This year, we will conclude our study on how we can enhance the provision of criminal legal aid, including the coverage in terms of means criteria and offences, and the possibility of setting up a Public Defender's Office.

sections.label: New means test criteria for legal aid
sections.summary: New means test criteria for civil legal aid introduced in October 2019 will be extended to CLAS this year, with eligible households maintained at 25%.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: We introduced new means test criteria for civil legal aid in October 2019, as I mentioned, aligned with those commonly used in social support schemes, namely: per capita household income; annual value; and the applicant's savings and non-CPF investments.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: This year, we will extend the new means test criteria for CLAS as well.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: There will be no material impact on the overall number of households eligible, we will maintain it at 25%, there will be no drop.

sections.label: Framework for Conditional Fee Agreements
sections.summary: A framework for Conditional Fee Agreements will be introduced as an additional litigation funding option for international arbitration, domestic arbitration and certain SICC proceedings.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: Third, we will introduce a framework for Conditional Fee Agreements, or CFAs, to provide an additional litigation funding option for international arbitration, for domestic arbitration, and certain prescribed proceedings in the Singapore International Commercial Courts, or SICC.

sections.label: TADM bearing ECT enforcement costs
sections.summary: For low-wage workers, TADM will help to bear the costs of enforcing ECT orders.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: For low-wage workers, TADM will help to bear the costs of enforcing the ECT orders.

sections.label: Relief notifications and SIP figures
sections.summary: As of 23 February, over 8,600 relief notifications were served, about 117,000 cash grant notices issued, and more than 490 Notices of Negotiation lodged under SIP.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: As of 23 February this year, more than 8,600 notifications for relief have been served through MinLaw's electronic system.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: About 117,000 notices of cash grant have been issued under the rental relief framework.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: The SIP – which had commenced on 29 January this year – provides financially distressed micro and small companies, or MSCs, with a low-cost, faster and more efficient way of either exiting the business by way of liquidation, or finding a way to restructure their debts so that they can then proceed with the business, which remains viable.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: To date, more than 490 Notices of Negotiation were lodged and served via the online electronic system.

sections.label: Landlord hardship rental waiver application
sections.summary: The framework lets landlords apply for assessment on hardship grounds to halve their share of rental waivers.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: Nonetheless, to recognise the need to balance the interests of landlords as well, the framework allows landlords to make an application for assessment on the grounds of hardship, to reduce their share of rental waivers by half.

sections.label: ITLOS Model Agreement Singapore
sections.summary: In June 2020 Singapore adopted a Model Agreement with ITLOS to host ITLOS proceedings in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: In June 2020, we adopted a Model Agreement with the International Tribunal for the Law of the Sea (ITLOS) to host ITLOS proceedings in Singapore.

sections.label: Apostille Convention and Hague Service Convention
sections.summary: After the Apostille Bill passed, Singapore joined the Apostille Convention in January 2021 and is studying acceding to the Hague Service Convention.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: With the passing of the Apostille Bill in November 2020, we became a party to the Apostille Convention in January 2021.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: Mr Pillai also asked for my Ministry’s position on the Hague Service Convention, which is a major international treaty that facilitates and also streamlines the transmission of judicial and extrajudicial documents for service abroad in civil and commercial matters.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: We are currently studying the possibility of acceding to the Convention.

sections.label: Singapore Convention on Mediation implementation
sections.summary: Singapore introduced the Singapore Convention on Mediation Act and Rules, and with UNCITRAL held a digital event marking the Convention's entry into force.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: It continues to be a mark of pride for us.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: We have since introduced the Singapore Convention on Mediation Act and its Rules to implement the domestic legal framework for the Convention.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: To commemorate the entry into force of the Convention on 12 September 2020, we jointly organised a digital event with the UN Commission on International Trade Law (UNCITRAL) involving the six countries, including Singapore, that had deposited their respective instruments of ratification or approval.

sections.label: SIAC New York office opening
sections.summary: SIAC opened its fifth international representative office in New York in December 2020.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: SIAC opened its fifth international representative office in New York in December 2020.

sections.label: MinLaw MOU with CCPIT
sections.summary: MinLaw signed an MOU with the China Council for the Promotion of International Trade at last year's JCBC meeting.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: MinLaw has also signed an MOU with the China Council for the Promotion of International Trade at the sidelines of last year's Singapore-China Joint Council for Bilateral Cooperation or JCBC meeting.

sections.label: SIAC and SIMC case numbers
sections.summary: As of 30 October 2020, SIAC received 1,005 cases, surpassing 1,000 for the first time, while SIMC received a record 43 cases in 2020.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: As of 30 October 2020, SIAC received 1,005 cases, including two sets of related cases, surpassing the 1,000 mark for the first time.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: SIMC, a much younger institution, also received a record 43 cases in 2020.

sections.label: Patent protection within six months
sections.summary: Under this programme, patent protection can be secured within six months.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: For instance, under this programme, patent protection can be secured within six months.

sections.label: Tech-celerate for Law support
sections.summary: MinLaw partnered Law Society for workshops and demos, extended Tech-celerate for Law, raised support to 80%, and 233 law practices benefited as of 14 September 2020.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: We have partnered Law Society to implement a series of workshops, roadshows and technology demos to basically build awareness, raise awareness, and to socialise lawyers with devices and platforms that they might otherwise not be familiar with.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: We extended the period of support for the funding scheme Tech-celerate for Law and enhanced support rates from 70% to 80% in 2020.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: As of 14 September 2020, a total of 233 law practices have benefited under the scheme and its predecessor – Tech Start for Law – to adopt technology in its practices.

sections.label: Integrated Legal Tech Platform plan
sections.summary: The Ministry is planning to develop an integrated Legal Tech Platform that unifies law firms' existing technology tools as far as possible.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: As such, my Ministry is planning to develop an integrated Legal Tech Platform that unifies law firms’ existing technology tools as far as possible.

sections.label: Industry Digital Plan development
sections.summary: MinLaw is working with IMDA and industry partners to develop an Industry Digital Plan giving lawyers a step-by-step guide to digital readiness and technology solutions.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: MinLaw is also working with IMDA and industry partners to develop an Industry Digital Plan which will – provide a step-by-step guide for lawyers to assess their digital readiness and to identify suitable technology solutions to adopt at each stage of their growth.

sections.label: Law student curriculum and training
sections.summary: MinLaw will work with institutions to finetune the curriculum and will implement changes to the practice training regime in 2023.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: As for law students and fresh graduates: we will continue to work with the institutions to finetune the curriculum to ensure that law students are well-equipped to meet the changing demands of the legal practice which I think Members will appreciate, especially the lawyers amongst us, which are changing very quickly.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: And this will also include changes to the practice training regime, which MinLaw has accepted in principle, and will be working with stakeholders to implement in 2023.

sections.label: Singapore Jiangsu Cooperation Council corridor
sections.summary: The Singapore Jiangsu Cooperation Council is to be used to develop an Internationalisation Corridor driving collaborations between Chinese enterprises and professional services firms, focusing on legal and accounting firms.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: Apart from initiatives outlined above, one other area to leverage on is the Singapore Jiangsu Cooperation Council (SJCC) to develop an Internationalisation Corridor.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: It aims to drive collaborations between Chinese enterprises and professional services firms, with a focus on legal and accounting firms.

sections.label: Digitisation of HDB leases
sections.summary: Since 2016, SLA has embarked on digitising about a million HDB leases, most of which have now been digitised.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: Since 2016, SLA has embarked on the digitisation of about a million HDB leases – most of which have now been digitised.

sections.label: iLAB language navigation and facilities
sections.summary: iLAB cannot currently be navigated in different languages, but other facilities such as the concierge and front staff counter can address other languages, and enhancing iLAB will be looked at.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: As I understand it, currently, you are not able to currently navigate iLAB in different languages.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: Nonetheless, if a litigant in person or a litigant who is looking at commencing a claim needs to find resources in other languages, there are other facilities available such as the concierge, the front staff counter, all of whom will be able to address other languages.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: We will look at the possibility of enhancing iLAB to deal with other languages.

sections.label: Assessors for small landlord disputes
sections.summary: The framework was designed to use Assessors rather than a strict legalistic adjudicatory process, allowing an Assessor to take into account factors a court might not.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: On his first point on small landlords, I would like to assure Mr de Souza that it is precisely with deftness in mind that the framework was designed; to use Assessors and not to use a strict legalistic adjudicatory process.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: And in the context of looking at a dispute between a landlord and a tenant, or two parties who have filed a notification, the Assessor can take into account factors which a court or a judge sitting in an adjudicatory process might not otherwise be able to do.

sections.label: Legal Aid Bureau iLAB pilot
sections.summary: A pilot project is a collaboration between the Legal Aid Bureau and community legal clinics, where volunteer lawyers use iLAB to provide preliminary legal advice to residents in need.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: What I also understand is that there is already a pilot project that is a collaboration between the Legal Aid Bureau in relation to the iLAB where it collaborates with our community legal clinics.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: The volunteer lawyers are able to use this system to provide the necessary preliminary legal advice to residents in need.

sections.label: Widening law graduates' training places
sections.summary: It is suggested that the Ministry explore widening the scope of places where law graduates can serve their training contract, including adding the Law Society Pro Bono Services.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: One is in relation to opening more opportunities for our law students and our law graduates, whether the Ministry can explore widening the scope of the places where law graduates can serve their training contract.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: In this regard, I think it will be helpful if we can consider adding places such as the Law Society Pro Bono Services as one of them.
